---
title: "Config"
---

The `config` block contains table-level metadata used for validation and rendering.

## Fields

<!-- ir-fields: Config -->

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `table_cols` | integer | required | Number of columns |
| `header_rows` | integer | `0` | Number of rows in `thead` |
| `body_rows` | integer | `0` | Number of data rows across all row groups (summary rows not counted) |
| `stub_cols` | integer | `0` | Number of stub (row label) columns, at the left |
| `row_striping` | boolean | `false` | Stripe alternate data rows ([below](#row-striping)) |
| `row_striping_include_stub` | boolean | `false` | Stripe the stub cells |
| `row_striping_include_body` | boolean | `false` | Stripe the other cells |
| `column_labels_hidden` | boolean | `false` | Leave out the column labels: every format draws an empty head |
| `table_width` | length? | `null` | The table's width: a length, or a % of the line ([widths](columns.qmd#width-values)) |
| `container_width` | length? | `null` | HTML: the most the container around the table is wide (`max-width`) |
| `container_height` | length? | `null` | HTML: the most the container is high (`max-height`) |
| `container_overflow` | keyword? | `null` | HTML: what the container does with a table that doesn't fit (`overflow`: `visible`, `hidden`, `clip`, `scroll` or `auto`) |
| `locale` | string | `"en-US"` | The locale the producer formatted values in. HTML takes its document's `lang` from it when `lang` isn't set |
| `lang` | string? | `null` | The language of the table's text, a BCP 47 tag ([language and direction](#language-and-direction)) |
| `dir` | keyword? | `null` | `"ltr"`, `"rtl"` or `"auto"`: the direction its columns and text run in |
| `page_break_mode` | keyword | `"avoid"` | `"avoid"`, `"allow"` or `"force-between-groups"`. Validated, but not yet read by any writer |
| `aria_label` | string? | `null` | HTML: the table's accessible name (`aria-label`), in place of the title |
| `aria_describedby` | string? | `null` | HTML: the ids of the elements that describe the table (`aria-describedby`), in place of the subtitle |
| `summary` | string? | `null` | HTML: a `<caption>` for the table, which then names it in place of the title |

## Row striping

With `row_striping`, even data rows (the 2nd, 4th, … counting across all row groups,
as gt does) get a 5% gray background, `rgba(128, 128, 128, 0.05)`. Stub cells are
striped when `row_striping_include_stub` is set and other cells when
`row_striping_include_body` is set, so with both flags off nothing is striped. Head and
summary rows are never striped. Striping sits below conditional, row and cell styles
in the [style cascade](styles.qmd#how-styles-combine), so any of them can override it.
Formats without transparency show the stripe as it looks on white (`#F9F9F9`).

## Language and direction

`lang` is the language the table's text is in, as a BCP 47 tag (`"ar"`, `"fr-CA"`,
`"zh-Hant-TW"`). It lets a format choose fonts, hyphenation and shaping for the text,
and screen readers choose a voice. A value that isn't a well-formed tag is an
[`INVALID_LANG`](validation.qmd#structural-rules) error. Unlike `locale`, which only sets how
values were formatted, `lang` is written into the output.

`dir` is the direction the table runs in. With `"rtl"`, the first column is on the
right, text runs right to left, and lines outside the grid (the title, group labels,
notes) start on the right. `"auto"` is right to left when the table's first strongly
directional character (in its title, labels and cells, in that order) is from a
right-to-left script such as Arabic or Hebrew. HTML leaves that to the browser. `"ltr"`
says left to right outright. Without `dir`, the table is left to right as before.
The direction is never inferred from `lang`, so an Arabic-language table without `dir`
still runs left to right.

Alignment and borders stay **physical** in either direction. A `left`-aligned column
is aligned left and a cell's `left` border is drawn on its left, wherever the cell
ends up. To make a column start-aligned in a right-to-left table, align it `right`.
How each format expresses this is listed under [output formats](../guide/output-formats.qmd#language-and-direction).

```json
{
  "config": {
    "table_cols": 3,
    "header_rows": 1,
    "body_rows": 4,
    "lang": "ar",
    "dir": "rtl"
  }
}
```

## Example

```json
{
  "config": {
    "table_cols": 5,
    "header_rows": 2,
    "body_rows": 10,
    "stub_cols": 1,
    "row_striping": true,
    "row_striping_include_stub": true,
    "row_striping_include_body": true,
    "column_labels_hidden": false,
    "table_width": "100%",
    "container_width": "900px",
    "locale": "en-US",
    "page_break_mode": "avoid"
  }
}
```

::: {.callout-note}
`body_rows` counts **data rows only** — summary rows are not included.
Stub columns must be contiguous starting from column 0.
:::
